title: Headlines & colour
slide_intent: Show how the color of text and its immediate box determine whether a headline stays readable across backgrounds. Changing the surrounding field creates a useful comparison.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can give its strongest hues different roles while the same word remains distinguishable over color or photography.
demonstration: Six groups demonstrate the three bright headlines on black and their inverse arrangements. A smaller set of crossed examples shows incorrect combinations.
practical_value: Choose a permitted type-and-box pair, then compare it on the actual page background or photograph.

content_islands.name: Pairing matrix
content_islands.spec: Arrange three columns across two rows. Put light-catching color on a black box in the top row and reverse the roles in the lower row.

content_islands.name: Background variations
content_islands.spec: Within each group repeat the same boxed word on several colored fields and a photograph so viewers can compare surrounding contrast.

content_islands.name: Excluded combinations
content_islands.spec: Set a compact stack of incorrect swatches beneath the explanation at lower left. Attach the caution and pink cross to that group.
